title: Spatial Data Management on AWS
description: In this advanced-level course, you explore the Spatial Data Management on AWS solution and learn how to plan, deploy, operate, and maintain it in your AWS account. title: Beyond Monitoring: Building Agentic SOC with Amazon Quick
description:

This course provides a practical introduction to building an agentic Security Operations Center (SOC) teammate on AWS using Amazon Quick Suite, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and Strands Agents (an open-source agent framework maintained by AWS). The session opens with the SOC scaling gap: alert volumes keep rising while SOC headcount does not, leaving many teams stuck routing alerts rather than running real security operations.

We examine why an AI-enabled teammate is the right answer — one that: \
• Correlates findings across Amazon GuardDuty, AWS CloudTrail, and Amazon VPC Flow Logs \
• Validates them against a centralized security data lake (e.g., Amazon Security Lake or a customer-managed log store) \
• Recommends remediation while keeping analysts in command

Participants will see a demonstration in which the agent triages a non-synthetic GuardDuty finding from a sandbox account, enriches it via Amazon Athena, and proposes containment through AWS Systems Manager Documents — all gated by human approval. The session also covers how Amazon Quick Suite, Bedrock AgentCore, and Strands extend with custom tools and Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations to connect your Configuration Management Database (CMDB), security data lake, and response playbooks, and closes with a working blueprint and code references that participants can adapt to their own environment.
objectives: Describe the SOC scaling gap and the case for agentic operations / Identify the roles of Amazon Quick Suite, Bedrock AgentCore, and Strands Agents in an agentic SOC architecture / Explain how an agent correlates findings, validates with data lake context, and recommends remediation / Recognize how custom tools and MCP integrations connect a CMDB, security data lake, and response playbooks / Describe human-in-the-loop control patterns for containment actions / Discuss business value and SOC capability improvements (aligned to the SOC-CMM framework)
audience: Chief Information Security Officers (CISOs) / SOC Leaders and Managers / SOC Analysts (Tier 1, Tier 2, Tier 3) / Incident Response Teams / Detection Engineers and Threat Hunters / Security Engineers building automation and SOAR workflows / Cloud Security Engineers
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with the AWS Management Console and a general awareness of SOC workflows (alert triage, response) • No prior experience with AI agents or the specific security services in the demo is required — the session is designed to make agentic security accessible to anyone curious about applying AI to SOC operations.

title: AI for Everyone: Your First Practical Steps
description:
This self-paced course gives people with no technical background a working understanding of
what AI is, where it lives, and how to use it. Learners move through eight short lessons at their
own pace, each built around a single idea and a hands-on practice activity. The practice
activities use a live interface powered by Claude, Anthropic's AI model running on Amazon Web
Services, so learners work with a real tool throughout the course rather than watching someone
else use one.
By the end of this digital course, learners know how to write a prompt that gets useful results,
understand the relationship between AI and cloud infrastructure in plain terms, and have a
personal plan for where AI fits into their work and daily routines. A points-based scoring system
tracks progress across all lessons, and a five-question assessment at the end unlocks the
course completion badge.
objectives: Explain what AI is, how it works, and why so many AI tools exist today / Describe what cloud computing is, what AWS is, and why AI runs on cloud infrastructure / Write prompts that produce useful results using the four-question method / Identify at least three places in your work or personal life where AI would save real time / Recognise situations where AI output should not be trusted without checking

title: Mitigating Adversarial Prompting with Amazon Bedrock
description:
*This course was developed by members of AWS Technical Field Communities (TFC), an AWS community of technical experts. The content is intended to complement our standard training curriculum and augment your AWS learning journey. We are aware some courses have accessibility limitations and are working to address. If you require accommodation, please contact [AWS Training and Certification Customer Support](https://support.aws.amazon.com/#/contacts/aws-training).*

This course introduces adversarial prompting techniques that exploit generative AI models and demonstrates how to defend against them using Amazon Bedrock. Participants will learn to identify six common adversarial techniques — persona switching, system prompt extraction, alternating languages and escape characters, fake completion attacks, rephrasing and obfuscation, and exploiting sycophancy. The course then introduces two key defense mechanisms: System Prompts for model behaviour control and Guardrails for external policy enforcement. Through a hands-on demonstration, attendees will observe how each attack succeeds against an unprotected model, how system prompts partially mitigate the attacks, and how a Defense in Depth pipeline combining system prompts and Amazon Bedrock Guardrails provides robust protection against adversarial attempts. The training emphasizes understanding the practical application of Amazon Bedrock's safety features for generative AI applications. This is a Level 200 course.
objectives: Define adversarial prompting and identify six common adversarial techniques used to exploit generative AI models / Describe the role of System Prompts in controlling model behaviour and mitigating adversarial attacks / Summarize Amazon Bedrock Guardrails' features: content filters, denied topics, word filters, sensitivity checks, contextual grounding, and automated reasoning checks / Explain how a Defense in Depth approach combining System Prompts and Guardrails provides layered protection for generative AI applications
aws_services: Amazon Bedrock / Amazon SageMaker
audience: Cloud Engineers and Architects exploring generative AI safety / Application Developers integrating generative AI into workloads / Solutions Architects evaluating AI safety strategies / Security Engineers interested in AI application safety / Technical Decision Makers assessing AI governance options / Anyone interested in understanding how to protect generative AI models from adversarial attacks

title: Kiro: Frontier Agent for Every Persona
description:
*This course was developed by members of AWS Technical Field Communities (TFC), an AWS community of technical experts. The content is intended to complement our standard training curriculum and augment your AWS learning journey. We are aware some courses have accessibility limitations and are working to address. If you require accommodation, please contact [AWS Training and Certification Customer Support](https://support.aws.amazon.com/#/contacts/aws-training).*

Most engineering teams already have an AI assistant. Fewer have worked out how to make it behave like a colleague who knows their codebase, their conventions, and their cloud account. That gap is what this course is about.

**Kiro** is an agentic AI development environment available across three surfaces: the **Kiro IDE**, **Kiro Web**, and the **Kiro CLI**. This course walks through the capabilities that let you shape how a Kiro agent works, then shows the same agent applied to three different jobs by three different personas.

The first half covers the mechanics. You will see how Kiro handles context: native **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** integration to reach docs, databases, and APIs; **steering files** to set how agents behave per project; and image input, so a photo of a whiteboard architecture session or a screenshot of a UI design can guide implementation. You will see **agent hooks**, which delegate work to agents that fire on events such as a file save and run autonomously in the background to generate documentation, write unit tests, or optimize performance. On the CLI side, **custom agents** narrow an agent to a specific job with pre-approved tool permissions, context files, and prompts, while **headless execution** runs Kiro programmatically inside a CI/CD pipeline with no user input, authenticating via API keys, device codes, or PKCE.

The course then covers **Kiro powers**, launched at re:Invent 2025, which extend agent capabilities through sharable best practices. A power can bundle MCP servers for access, steering files for context, and hooks for actions. Powers come from ISVs such as Figma, Postman, and Stripe, from domain experts packaging specialized use cases, and from community members sharing their own from GitHub. 

Alongside powers you will see how **skills** work: a folder containing a SKILL.md with YAML frontmatter and Markdown instructions, loaded progressively so only lightweight metadata sits in context until a task matches the skill's description. The section closes with a side-by-side comparison of **skills**, **steering**, **and MCP**: what each provides, when each loads, what triggers it, and what each is best for. They are complementary rather than competing.

The second half is applied, one section per persona.

**Developer.** Two scenarios: asking Kiro to locate where item validation happens during checkout in an unfamiliar project, made faster by steering; and asking Kiro to deploy an application into an AWS account.

**DevOps.** Reviewing an Amazon ECS service and an Amazon RDS instance for right-sizing, using subagents running in parallel.

**Security Operations.** The largest section, built on a deliberately small architecture: a single SKILL.md acting as a security operations analyst persona that routes to three workflows, sharing one definition of the MCP data source, grounding discipline, safety rules, and a standard ticket-ready output format. The pattern is three steps: MCP gathers the evidence by calling live AWS APIs, the skill reasons over it using expert workflow logic, and Kiro drafts the work product you would otherwise write by hand. It is read-only by default and confirms before any mutating action. Three use cases are presented and then run live:\
• **Investigate security events** with Amazon GuardDuty: pull the finding, enrich the actor identity, scope blast radius through AWS CloudTrail, classify true or false positive, recommend containment, and draft a triage note\
• **Remediate weak configuration** with AWS Security Hub CSPM: pull failed controls, prioritize by severity and exposure, confirm resource state, propose the fix, apply it, then re-check that the control actually passed\
• **Implement least privilege** with AWS IAM Access Analyzer: pull unused-access findings, review real CloudTrail activity, generate a refined policy from what the role actually did, produce a current-versus-proposed diff, and draft guidance for the resource owner

One caveat is stated plainly in the session: this is an analyst assistant. It does not replace your SIEM and it does not perform real-time streaming detection. Its value is in the investigation, remediation, and documentation work that surrounds a finding that already exists.

The course closes with the **Agentic AI Security Scoping Matrix**, a four-scope model spanning human-initiated with no agency through automated initiation with full agency, used to reason about how security requirements scale as you hand an agent more autonomy, and where current agentic AWS tooling, Kiro included, sits on it.
objectives: Identify the three surfaces through which Kiro is accessed: Kiro IDE, Kiro Web, and Kiro CLI / Describe how Kiro manages context using native MCP integration, steering files, and image input / Explain how agent hooks delegate work to agents that trigger on events and execute autonomously in the background / Describe how CLI custom agents scope an agent with pre-approved tool permissions, context files, and prompts, and how headless execution runs Kiro inside a CI/CD pipeline / Explain what a Kiro power is and the three things it can bundle: MCP servers for access, steering files for context, and hooks for actions / Differentiate skills, steering, and MCP by what they provide, how they load, what triggers them, and what each is best suited to / Describe the structure of a skill, including SKILL.md frontmatter requirements and progressive loading / Apply Kiro to developer, DevOps, and security operations tasks using the demonstrated scenarios / Describe the security operations pattern where MCP gathers evidence, the skill reasons over it, Kiro drafts the output with read-only-by-default and confirm-before-mutating safety defaults. / Walk the investigation, remediation, and least privilege workflows built on Amazon GuardDuty, AWS Security Hub CSPM, and AWS IAM Access Analyzer / Use the Agentic AI Security Scoping Matrix to reason about how security requirements scale with an agent's initiation model and level of agency

title: Introduction to DynamoDB Bulk Put Items
description:
Amazon DynamoDB Bulk Put Items is a fully managed feature that imports data from Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) into an existing DynamoDB table. The import runs on a separate write path, so it consumes none of your table's read or write capacity and does not compete with your live application traffic.
In this course, you explore what the feature does, how a bulk operation runs from start to finish, and the four API actions you use to control it. You compare the Standard and Accelerated performance tiers so you can match speed and cost to your workload. You also learn when to choose bulk put items over building your own pipeline, and how to prepare your data and table for the best results.

This course teaches learners how to build an automated "Burst to Region" pattern for AWS Outposts. When an Outposts rack runs out of compute capacity, this pattern detects the constraint, launches EC2 instances in the parent AWS Region, shifts traffic to them, and returns traffic locally once capacity recovers. Learners gain hands-on experience configuring CloudWatch, SNS, Lambda, EC2 Auto Scaling, Application Load Balancer, and EventBridge to implement this overflow automation. The course also covers when this pattern is appropriate -- primarily for stateless or latency-tolerant workloads that prefer local capacity but can gracefully handle moderate latency increases during peak demand.
objectives: Design and implement a Burst to Region pattern that automatically overflows AWS Outposts workloads to Amazon EC2 instances in the parent AWS Region during capacity constraints / Configure and operate six AWS services—CloudWatch, SNS, Lambda, EC2 Auto Scaling, ALB, and EventBridge—to automate capacity detection, overflow scaling, traffic distribution, and recovery

description:
This short course introduces Strands Box, an open source sandbox for governing what AI agents do. Across five lessons you will see why agent autonomy creates a new kind of risk, how Box combines operating-system containment with fine-grained policy, where it enforces that policy, and how Dogwood policies can reason about what an agent has already done. There are no hands-on labs: Box is in developer preview, so the goal is to understand the model and the vocabulary, not to configure a production system.

**What you will be able to do by the end:**

- Explain why isolation alone does not fully govern an autonomous agent.
- Describe the two layers inside Strands Box — containment and policy.
- Identify the four enforcement points and how the egress gateway handles credentials.
- Explain, in plain terms, what a temporal (history-aware) policy does.
- Recall where a Box configuration runs and what ships next.

*This course was developed by members of AWS Technical Field Communities (TFC), an AWS community of technical experts. The content is intended to complement our standard training curriculum and augment your AWS learning journey. We are aware some courses have accessibility limitations and are working to address. If you require accommodation, please contact [AWS Training and Certification Customer Support](https://support.aws.amazon.com/#/contacts/aws-training).*

Learners will gain insight into the challenges of running large-scale, multi-tenant ad-serving infrastructure on AWS -- including inefficiencies of cellular architecture such as low resource utilization, lengthy client onboarding, scaling limitations, and noisy neighbor issues. The course covers how to design a hybrid multi-tenant architecture for stateful services that balances tenant isolation with operational efficiency, reduces costs from idle infrastructure, accelerates onboarding timelines, and supports concurrent high-traffic events across multiple tenants and regions.
objectives: Design and implement a hybrid multi-tenant architecture using Amazon ECS that provides cluster-level tenant isolation within shared AWS accounts / Reduce tenant onboarding time from weeks to hours by implementing configuration-driven infrastructure with tiered architecture, Route 53 weighted routing, shared AWS PrivateLink connectivity
aws_services: Amazon Elastic Container Service
roles: Application Architect / Architect / DevOps Engineer / Infrastructure Engineer / Network Architect / Developer

title: Building Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) workflows with Amazon OpenSearch Service
description: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) is a powerful technique that enhances the accuracy and relevance of AI-generated responses by combining information retrieval with text generation. In this course, you will explore how to build RAG solutions using Amazon OpenSearch Service, a fully managed search and analytics solution. In this course you will discover how embeddings, which are vector representations of textual data, can significantly improve search and information retrieval capabilities. We will delve into the process of creating effective retrievers for RAG using the advanced features of Amazon OpenSearch Service. This course includes presentations, demonstrations, and assessments.
objectives: Explain the workflow of large language models (LLMs) and identify their limitations / Describe RAG and illustrate how it improves LLM performance / Identify and outline the steps involved in building a knowledge base for RAG / Compare different search methods that OpenSearch supports / Demonstrate the use of Amazon OpenSearch Serverless with Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases to generate embeddings and retrieve relevant information
aws_services: Amazon OpenSearch Service / Amazon Bedrock / Amazon Simple Storage Service
audience: Technical field community / Analytics solutions architects (SAs) / Database administrators / Database engineers / Data architects / Solutions architects (SAs) / Data platform engineers / Search specialists
prerequisites: A basic knowledge of OpenSearch Service or Amazon OpenSearch Serverless on the AWS. Completed the Level 100 course on Skill Builder for OpenSearch Service, Getting Started with Amazon OpenSearch Service. Completed the Level 200 course on Skill Builder for OpenSearch Service, Empower Search with AI using Amazon OpenSearch Service.

title: Moving to the Cloud with Amazon FSx
description: In this course, you will learn about why you should consider Amazon FSx when moving or extending your on-premises shared file storage to the cloud. You will also learn about which Amazon FSx offering could be ideal for your use case. It might be a complete migration, moving to the cloud for disaster recovery, or extending your on-premises compute and storage to the cloud to handle periods of peak demand. You will also learn how to prepare for moving your on-premises data into an Amazon FSx file system and understand the specific migration and hybrid considerations that go along with each individual Amazon FSx service offering. This course includes interactive lessons, demonstrations, and knowledge check questions.
objectives: Explain the financial and organizational benefits of moving to cloud file storage / Differentiate Amazon FSx from other types of Amazon Web Services (AWS) storage offerings / Identify the benefits of using Amazon FSx rather than do-it-yourself cloud file storage deployments / List the features of Amazon FSx that make it an optimal solution when you move to the cloud / Describe the potential relations between on-premises deployments and cloud deployments / Explain how to prepare and migrate to Amazon FSx
aws_services: Amazon FSx / AWS DataSync / Amazon Simple Storage Service
audience: Cloud architects / Storage and cloud operations administrators / Storage business development managers / Data engineers
prerequisites: We recommend that attendees of this course have: Getting Started with AWS Storage course, General knowledge of AWS and cloud computing

Learners will gain an understanding of how vector databases support generative AI applications, particularly in leveraging proprietary domain-specific data to differentiate business strategies. The course covers how large language models and foundation models work at the core of generative AI, and explains how vector capabilities integrated into existing database services can simplify application architecture. Participants will also learn about AWS solutions that enable organizations to harness generative AI using familiar tools and skills, allowing them to move quickly without overhauling their data infrastructure.

title: Build an AI Recommendation Engine Step by Step (Graph + Bedrock)
description:
Couldn't join us live? Stream the full recording and learn at your own pace.

Most recommendation tutorials start with "first, build an ML pipeline." But your data already contains the relationships you need. They're just trapped in rows and columns.

In this hands-on session, we're taking real Yelp review data and walking through the full path from flat files to a working recommendation engine you can query in plain English. Bedrock, Opensearch, and Neptune, — zero to done.
objectives: How to look at any tabular dataset and spot the entities and relationships hiding in it / How to transform flat data into a queryable graph without writing complex ETL / How to layer natural language queries on top so you can ask your graph real questions / A mental model for when graph traversal beats traditional ML for recommendations
audience: You're a developer or data engineer who's built (or been asked to build) a "you might also like" feature / You've got tabular data and a nagging feeling there's a better way than throwing it all at an ML model / You want to understand when a problem is actually a graph problem vs. a similarity problem

title: AWS Storage Data Protection Services Getting Started
description: AWS Storage provides you with the services you need to build the storage solution that's right for your organization. Backup and disaster recovery services provide you those additional tools to develop your complete storage solutions. You will discover backup and service native snapshot services available for you to choose to meet your organization's backup requirements. You also discover an AWS service designed to replicate your on-premises application servers to provide disaster recovery protection. In addition, you learn about service native replication that you can you use to protect your data or enhance service availability across AWS Regions. You can select from these different service offerings and apply them to your organization's needs and determine the possible paths you can take to arrive at the best storage solution. Before choosing an AWS Storage solution, AWS recommends that you first assess what storage characteristics are appropriate for your applications and business. After familiarizing yourself with AWS Storage, you can then compare your requirements to the available AWS Storage services and select the solution that meets your needs. This course introduces customers to the benefits, features, use cases, and considerations for storage data protection services including AWS Backup and AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery services. In addition, you are introduced to other storage protections services that are native features included with the core block, file, and object services. These include snapshots and replication features. This course includes: Online materials, demonstrations, and knowledge check questions.
objectives: Recognize and recall the AWS Storage Data Protection services / Discuss AWS Backup service / Define service native snapshot services / Discuss AWS DRS service

title: Introduction to Credits, Savings Plans and Reserved Instances Sharing
description:
Companies that use cost saving benefits like Credits, Savings Plans and Reserved Instances often want savings to stay with the teams that owns them. By default, any part of a benefit that the owning account does not use goes to other accounts in the organization. This gets the most optimal savings, but it can create chargeback problems.
In this course, you learn how benefit sharing works by default. You learn how group sharing and level sharing give you control over credits, Savings Plans and Reserved Instances. You also learn how to choose between Prioritized and Restricted sharing modes.

title: Digital Sovereignty on AWS
description:
Organizations are facing increasing complexity in an evolving sovereignty landscape. As a result, you may be concerned with how to remain compliant and acquire the right tools and services without sacrificing the benefits of working in the cloud. In this course, you will learn the key concepts of digital sovereignty, including digital sovereignty themes, examples of sovereignty requirements, and typical challenges and questions. You will also discover how the AWS Cloud is sovereign-by-design and learn how Amazon Web Services (AWS) is helping you address your complex and evolving requirements. This course will also dive into an example use case using a fictitious customer that is expanding their operations. You will analyze how to build a sovereign-by-design solution while accounting for compliance, control, and continuity. Through this use case, you will also learn how AWS services can help address specific requirements. 

Course level: Intermediate. 

Course duration: 120 minutes.
objectives: Explain the concept of digital sovereignty and how Amazon Web Services (AWS) is sovereign-by-design. / Summarize how AWS delivers on the four pillars of the AWS Digital Sovereignty Pledge. / Describe the integration of compliance, control, and continuity in creating a sovereign-by-design workload. / Analyze how to build sovereign-by-design solutions that account for compliance, control, and continuity. / Correlate AWS services to your use case in a sovereign-by-design solution.

audience: Architects
prerequisites: AWS Technical Essentials
roles: Security Engineer / Network Architect / Infrastructure Engineer

title: Customizing and Evaluating LLMs Using Amazon SageMaker JumpStart
description: In this course, you learn about customizing and evaluating large language models (LLMs) using Amazon SageMaker JumpStart. Amazon SageMaker JumpStart is a machine learning (ML) hub with foundation models, built-in algorithms, and prebuilt ML solutions that you can deploy with a few clicks. You will learn the alternatives to fine-tuning including the foundations of prompt engineering and retrieval augmented generation (RAG). You will also learn to fine-tune, deploy and evaluate fine-tuned models available on SageMaker JumpStart. Using your own AWS account and the notebooks provided, you can practice building RAG applications using the Amazon SageMaker-LangChain integration. You can also fine-tune a Llama3 model and evaluate it using evaluation metrics. You can practice one of the aspects of responsible AI with the help of a notebook that addresses prompt stereotyping. Alternatively, you can watch a video demonstration of running the notebooks. Course level: Advanced. Duration: 4 hours. This course includes presentations, demonstrations, and assessments.
objectives: Describe the different techniques to customize LLMs. / Describe when to use prompt engineering and retrieval augmented generation as customization options. / Demonstrate the use of Amazon SageMaker-LangChain integration to build a RAG application using a Falcon model. / Describe the use of domain adaptation and instruction fine-tuning. / Demonstrate how to fine-tune and deploy a model from the SageMaker JumpStart ML hub. / Demonstrate the use of the SageMaker Python SDK to fine-tune LLMs using Parameter Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT). / Evaluate foundation models by using the SageMaker JumpStart console and fmeval library.

description:

This course explores the essential maintenance and upgrade strategies for Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL and Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL databases. You'll learn about different maintenance operations and their impact on database availability. The course covers Automatic Minor Version Upgrades (AMVU) and Aurora's Zero Downtime Patching (ZDP) capabilities. You'll discover various approaches for major version upgrades, including in-place upgrades, logical replication methods, Blue/Green deployments, and using AWS Database Migration Service (DMS). These techniques are applicable to both Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL and Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL, with specific considerations for each service highlighted. By examining best practices for major version upgrades, you'll learn to plan and execute database upgrades while minimizing downtime and maintaining data integrity. This practical course is designed to help database administrators effectively manage the lifecycle of their PostgreSQL databases on both Aurora and RDS platforms.
objectives: Understand and implement different maintenance operations in Aurora and RDS PostgreSQL, including AMVU and Zero Downtime Patching / Execute and troubleshoot major version upgrades using various strategies, including in-place upgrades and logical replication / Configure and utilize pglogical extension for upgrade processes / Implement Blue/Green deployments and use AWS Database Migration Service (DMS) for version upgrades / Plan, execute, and monitor maintenance windows and upgrade processes effectively / Analyze upgrade pre-check logs, resolve common issues, and apply best practices for major version upgrades / Evaluate and choose appropriate upgrade strategies based on specific database requirements

title: AWS Transform for mainframe - Beyond the Basics
description:
*This course was developed by members of AWS Technical Field Communities (TFC), an AWS community of technical experts. The content is intended to complement our standard training curriculum and augment your AWS learning journey. We are aware some courses have accessibility limitations and are working to address. If you require accommodation, please contact [AWS Training and Certification Customer Support](https://support.aws.amazon.com/#/contacts/aws-training).*

This course equips participants with the skills to use AWS Transform for mainframe modernization. Learn to prepare mainframe assets (COBOL, JCL, CICS, BMS, DB2, VSAM) in Amazon S3, launch modernization jobs via the web experience, and interpret analysis dashboards. You will learn to generate functional documentation, extraction of business rules, and experience refactoring COBOL and JCL to Java and Groovy while maintaining functional equivalence, and learn to apply Reforge for improved code readability and maintainability.

Course objectives 
1. Explain the agent‑orchestrated workflow AWS Transform employs to migrate mainframe workloads. 
2. Prepare mainframe assets (COBOL, JCL, CICS, BMS, DB2, VSAM) in Amazon S3 for analysis. 
3. Launch & configure a comprehensive modernization job from the web console. 
4. Interpret analysis dashboards (file metrics, dependencies, gaps, duplicates).

description:
This 60-minute advanced course explores how Amazon Nova Forge's data mixing capability solves the catastrophic forgetting problem that plagues fine-tuned large language models. Through a real-world case study classifying over 16,000 customer comments across 1,420 categories, you'll see how full-rank supervised fine-tuning delivers a 17-point F1 improvement but devastates general capabilities — and how blending proprietary data with Nova-curated training data preserves near-baseline intelligence while still achieving strong domain performance. 

The course covers the fundamentals of PEFT versus full-rank SFT, walks through detailed benchmark results comparing Nova 2 Lite and Qwen3-30B, and provides practical recommendations for choosing the right fine-tuning approach based on your deployment needs. Through knowledge checks and real-world scenarios, you'll learn when to use data mixing versus customer-data-only fine-tuning, how to design dual evaluation frameworks, and how to deploy specialized models that don't sacrifice the general capabilities your enterprise workflows depend on.

title: Introduction to AWS Credit Split and Transfer
description:
In an AWS Organization, AWS issues a credit to one account. Sharing rules then decide which other accounts can use the amount that the account does not use. Until now, a customer with a large credit meant for several teams could not give each team its share directly.
Credit Split and Transfer lets you split a credit into portions and transfer each portion to a specific account in your organization. Each receiving account owns its portion and uses it on its own eligible usage first. In this course, you learn how split and transfer works, when to use it, and how to manage credits across accounts.

title: Cut Your LLM Costs and Latency up to 86% with Semantic Caching
description:
Many of your users ask the same question worded differently, and you're paying your LLM to answer every single one from scratch. Give your application a semantic cache to reuse answers for questions that mean the same thing for lower inference costs and faster responses.

If your AI project is stuck in prototype because the production cost doesn't work or your application latency gets worse with production traffic, this one's for you.

Traditional caches need exact string matches, which almost never happen with natural language. Semantic caching matches on meaning instead and the impact is staggering.

Build a semantic cache with Amazon ElastiCache (Valkey) that intercepts redundant LLM calls before they hit your model
See the real cost math: up to 86% reduction in LLM API costs & up to 88% faster response times
Learn how to tune similarity thresholds so your cache saves money without sacrificing generativeAI answer quality

title: Build RAG Without a Separate Vector DB — Amazon DocumentDB | Databases for AI
description:
Your team has thousands of pages of docs. Your developers still can't find the right answer. Join us to learn how to simplify search.

Blogs, PDFs, FAQs, developer guides—the knowledge exists. It's just buried. So your devs spend hours searching instead of minutes building. The fix sounds obvious: build a chatbot over it. But then you look at the typical RAG architecture & see two databases, a sync layer & a pile of glue code.

There's a simpler path. Amazon DocumentDB stores your vectors & your source content in the same document—so retrieval is one query to one place. No separate vector DB. No cross-database orchestration.

We walk through the full build:

⚡ Parse & embed PDFs, blogs & FAQs using Amazon SageMaker & #AmazonBedrock

⚡ Store embeddings alongside source data in DocumentDB—single collection, single document

⚡ Demo a working chatbot that handles everything from "show me the aggregation syntax" to "how do I migrate my Oracle workload to a document database?"

Collapse your #RAG architecture & give your devs a knowledge assistant they'll actually use. That's the power of #VectorSearch in a document database.

title: The Associate Cert Playbook: Your 12 month plan for all 5 Associate Certs
description:
Five AWS Associate certifications in 12 months sounds impossible—until you understand the overlap. In this 60-minute, previously recorded livestream, AWS Customer Solutions Manager Matt Jorat and reveals the certification roadmap he wished he had when he started: the Overlap Matrix.

What You'll Learn:
* The Overlap Matrix — Most certification pairs share 45–66% of content. SAA ↔ DEA: 62%. DEA ↔ MLA: 66%. SAA ↔ SOA: 61%.
* 24 Universal Services — These core AWS services appear on ALL five associate exams: EC2, Lambda, S3, VPC, IAM, KMS, DynamoDB, RDS, CloudWatch, CloudTrail, CloudFormation, SQS, SNS, Athena, EventBridge, Step Functions, Systems Manager, Secrets Manager, CloudFront, EBS, EFS, ECR, ECS, EKS.
* Study Strategies That Work — Take practice exams cold first. Study one domain per week. Analyze wrong answers AND right answers. Gamify with Cloud Quest, Card Clash, and SimuLearn.

title: AWS Continuum for Code Vulnerabilities: Finding and Proving Exploitable Risk
description:
AWS Continuum for Code Vulnerabilities is a continuous, AWS-infrastructure-aware code security service that uses frontier cyber-capable models to find, prove, and prioritize exploitable vulnerabilities in your first-party code. Rather than treating the model as the whole product, Continuum runs the model as one component inside an engineered system that reproduces each candidate exploit in an isolated sandbox and ranks it against your actual production context.
In this course, you will work through how that system is designed and how its four-stage loop — Discover, Prioritize, Validate, Remediate — produces findings an engineer can trust. You will analyze how attack paths are computed across services and how exploitability is proven against your own build. The emphasis is on why the architecture produces true positives, so you can reason about the output and position the service accurately in a security program.

title: Kiro Governance and Safety: Securing Agentic AI in Enterprises
description:
*This course was developed by members of AWS Technical Field Communities (TFC), an AWS community of technical experts. The content is intended to complement our standard training curriculum and augment your AWS learning journey. We are aware some courses have accessibility limitations and are working to address. If you require accommodation, please contact [AWS Training and Certification Customer Support](https://support.aws.amazon.com/#/contacts/aws-training).*

Agentic AI coding tools like **Kiro** move past autocomplete. Kiro is an agentic IDE and CLI, built on AWS, that turns prompts into specs, code, docs, and tests. To do that work it reads and writes files, runs commands, calls external tools through the **Model Context Protocol (MCP)**, and reaches into AWS resources. That reach is exactly what makes it productive for developers, and exactly why a careless enterprise rollout is dangerous. This course is the governance view: what an administrator, a security reviewer, and a developer working inside these controls all need to know before Kiro goes org-wide.

The course opens by framing why agentic coding changes the governance conversation. Spec-driven development with Kiro redistributes effort toward upfront planning and structured review, but the same speed that makes a team productive also raises the cost of a wrong action if boundaries are not in place first. Many organizations start with agentic coding as an individual experiment and then move to production at enterprise scale, and that transition is where governance becomes necessary rather than optional.

The core of the course maps every governance concern to the control that addresses it, using a running question to test each one: **can a developer simply turn this control off**. **Identity and access integration** authenticates enterprise users through AWS IAM Identity Center, Okta, or Microsoft Entra ID, with subscriptions assigned to users and groups rather than ad hoc logins, scoped by a Kiro profile of AWS account plus Region. **Subscription and license management** tracks credit and overage consumption per user from the same console. **MCP server governance** lets administrators disable MCP entirely or publish an HTTPS-hosted allow-list of approved servers that clients sync at startup and every 24 hours, terminating any locally installed server that drifts off the list, and failing closed if the client cannot reach the governance API. **Model governance** lets administrators curate an approved model list and set a default, which is curation rather than bring-your-own-model, with direct implications for data residency since generally available models use regional inference while experimental models may route globally. **Feature controls** add broader switches, including a web tools toggle that disables web search and fetch organization-wide.

The course then covers how governance creates visibility. The native usage dashboard shows aggregate metrics. A per-user activity report writes a daily CSV to an S3 bucket in your own account, and prompt logging records actual prompts and responses to your own bucket for audit and compliance, which means the data lives in your account and can feed your own Athena and QuickSight dashboards. On data handling, enterprise use means Kiro does not use your content for service improvement or model training and opts you out of telemetry automatically, and encrypts in transit and at rest by default. Content itself may still be stored in the Region where your profile is configured in order to provide the service, which is how prompt logging and activity reports operate. That leaves two real decisions: a customer-managed KMS key, and residency for experimental models.

The course closes on what lives outside the central console. **Steering files** give Kiro persistent rules as soft guidance. **Hooks** are enforceable: a PreToolUse command hook that exits with any non-zero code blocks the tool invocation outright, regardless of how the prompt was phrased. **Checkpoints and rewind** provide session recovery, with the important limit that checkpoints do not track changes made by MCP tools or by bash commands the agent runs. The course ends on the boundary that holds regardless of any client-side setting: Kiro holds no cloud credentials of its own and acts with whatever AWS credentials already exist in the developer's environment, so least-privilege IAM and short-lived sessions cap the blast radius no matter what a prompt, hook, or model attempts, because AWS enforces that boundary server-side. This distinction is load-bearing, because MCP and model governance are enforced client-side and can be circumvented by a user with local administrative access.
objectives: Explain why the speed and autonomy of agentic coding tools change the governance conversation compared to traditional developer tooling / Describe how a Kiro profile scopes governance by AWS account and Region, and how identity and access integration works through IAM Identity Center, Okta, or Microsoft Entra ID / Describe subscription and license management, including per-user credit and overage tracking / Explain MCP server governance: the allow-list registry model, the sync and drift-termination behavior, and the fail-closed default / Explain model governance as curation rather than bring-your-own-model, and its connection to data residency for generally available versus experimental models / Identify the organization-wide feature controls, including the web tools toggle / Describe the layered monitoring and visibility stack: the native dashboard, per-user activity reports, prompt logging, and custom dashboards built on your own data / Explain Kiro's enterprise data handling posture / Differentiate steering files as soft guidance from hooks as an enforceable block, where a non-zero exit code from a PreToolUse hook stops the tool call / Describe checkpoints and rewind as session recovery, including what checkpoints do not track / Explain why MCP and model governance are enforced client-side and can be circumvented locally
aws_services: Kiro / Amazon Simple Storage Service / Amazon Athena
audience: Software developers adopting Kiro and working inside enterprise governance controls / Security operations analysts and security reviewers evaluating agentic AI tools for rollout / Solutions architects and platform or enablement leads planning enterprise deployment / Cloud security engineers / Engineering and security leaders deciding how much autonomy to grant agentic tools and what controls to require first

title: Attaching Context to Your Data with Amazon S3 Annotations
description:
This short course introduces Amazon S3 annotations, a metadata capability that lets you attach rich, queryable business context directly to your S3 objects. Across five lessons you will see why object metadata is hard to manage today, what an annotation is and how it differs from tags and other metadata, how annotations behave across the object's lifecycle, and how to query them at scale. There are no hands-on labs: the goal is to understand what annotations are and when to reach for them, not to configure a production system.

What you will be able to do by the end:

* Explain the metadata problem that annotations are designed to solve.
* Describe what an S3 annotation is and its key limits.
* Distinguish annotations from object tags and user-defined metadata.
* Describe how annotations behave through copy, replication, update, and delete.
* Recall how annotations become queryable at scale.

title: AWS AI Business Strategist - Responsible AI Principles and Dimensions
description: Learn how to apply the responsible AI dimensions to described system scenarios, and choose a decision framework when business objectives conflict with those principles. You will also build governance into a project plan from the start rather than bolting it on, and judge which applications need human oversight and what safeguards they require.
objectives: Apply responsible AI dimensions (fairness, explainability, privacy, safety, transparency, robustness) to a described  AI system scenario / Distinguish the appropriate decision framework for a described conflict between business objectives and responsible AI principles / Apply governance-by-design practices to an AI project plan, differentiating from governance-as-afterthought approaches  / Distinguish which AI application scenarios require human oversight based on risk level, including appropriate safeguards (hallucination detection, guardrails, escalation criteria)

title: Amazon Quick: Data Modeling Patterns for Amazon Quick Sight Multi-Dataset Relationships
description: In this course, you learn how to implement specific data modeling patterns using Amazon Quick Sight multi-dataset relationships. You apply seven natively supported schema patterns with concrete table structures, SQL examples, and implementation steps. You also apply workarounds for advanced patterns including circular joins, recursive hierarchies, ragged hierarchies, and split hierarchies.

title: AI Traffic Monetization - Implementing Pay-Per-Access For AI Agents
description:
As AI agents and bots increasingly consume web content at scale, content owners face a critical challenge: how to monetize this machine-driven traffic without blocking legitimate AI use cases. AWS WAF AI Traffic Monetization solves this by enabling content and API providers to charge AI bots and agents for access to protected resources directly at the CDN edge, using the open x402 payment protocol and on-chain USDC settlement.

This course teaches cloud security engineers, infrastructure engineers, and solutions architects how to design, implement, and operate AI traffic monetization using AWS WAF, Amazon CloudFront, and the x402 protocol ecosystem.

title: How bitdrift scaled to 121 million concurrent gRPC connections on Amazon CloudFront for live telemetry sporting events
description:

Learners will discover how bitdrift scaled to 121 million concurrent gRPC connections during live T20 World Cup cricket broadcasts using Amazon CloudFront. The course covers how DNS routing policy choices -- specifically weighted versus multi-value answer routing -- can cause connection concentration on a single origin endpoint under extreme traffic surges. Participants will learn how bitdrift and the AWS account team diagnosed this imbalance and resolved it with a single DNS configuration change, enabling their multi-NLB architecture to distribute load evenly and serve all devices with zero server-side errors.
objectives: Design and implement a multi-origin Amazon CloudFront architecture using Route 53 Multi-Value Answer routing to distribute persistent gRPC connections across multiple Network Load Balancers / Diagnose and resolve DNS-driven traffic concentration issues that cause thundering herd effects when scaling to millions of concurrent connections on Amazon CloudFront

title: A leader's guide to advanced mental models and mechanisms - AWS re:Invent 2025
description:
In case you missed it at AWS re:Invent, join us for this previously recorded Leader's Guide discussion for executives.

To build a lasting, performant corporate culture, you need not only strong mental models to guide your employees and help them make decisions but also the right mechanisms to operationalize company values and mental models—and to help them persist. This session examines why organizational culture erodes over time, dives into the organizational artifacts that reinforce existing cultural patterns, and shares some of the best practices that help create strong mechanisms, using examples from Amazon’s own journey.

Through practical examples and hands-on guidance, you gain the skills to integrate Amazon SQS into your architectures, manage message lifecycle, and apply best practices for error handling and dead-letter queues. title: AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) Getting Started

title: AWS Security Agent - Get started with AI-powered proactive AppSec

title: Amazon Connect Agent Performance Evaluations

This intermediate-level training will equip you with the skills to effectively assess and improve contact center agent performance through thoughtful evaluation practices. This course is designed for quality assurance managers, contact center supervisors, and training coordinators who want to build more effective quality programs. title: Introduction to AWS Lambda MicroVMs

title: Build AI Agents That Remember: Agentic Memory with Valkey
description:
Your AI agent forgets everything the moment a conversation ends. Every session starts from scratch, requiring users to re-explain their needs each time. The problem isn't your model's intelligence — it's that your application lacks a memory layer.

In this course, you'll learn how to solve one of the most common challenges in building agentic AI applications: persistent memory. You'll explore the two types of agentic memory, build both using popular frameworks, and walk away with a reference architecture and working code you can plug into your existing AI stack.

By the end of this course, you'll be able to:

- Distinguish between short-term agent memory (session context and state) and long-term agent memory (facts and relationships), and know when each applies to your use case

- Add persistent memory to an agent using frameworks like LangGraph, Mem0, and Cognee, backed by Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey

- Apply a reference architecture and working code to integrate a memory layer into your existing AI stack — without rewriting your application

description:

If you require accommodation, please contact [AWS Training and Certification Customer Support](https://support.aws.amazon.com/#/contacts/one-support?formId=trainingCertification).*

Plenty of AWS Glue pipelines work in a tutorial and then struggle in production. This course closes that gap. You follow one fictional retailer's order data from raw ingestion to curated, governed analytics, and you build a Bronze, Silver, and Gold medallion architecture on Apache Iceberg along the way.

You start by ingesting new files incrementally with job bookmarks. Next you use MERGE INTO to handle late-arriving and changed orders. To protect data quality, you gate the Silver layer with AWS Glue Data Quality rules, then quarantine records that fail and replay them. You serve the Gold layer as AWS Glue Data Catalog materialized views, and you govern every layer with AWS Lake Formation LF-Tags and column-level security.

The course then covers running the pipeline day to day: monitoring, retries, runbooks, Iceberg table maintenance, and ways to lower cost. It targets AWS Glue 6.0 and includes notes for teams migrating from AWS Glue 5.1.
objectives: 1.	Design incremental data ingestion pipelines using Glue bookmarks and partition-based processing that handle late-arriving data and schema evolution gracefully. / 2.	Implement Lake Formation permission models (tag-based access control, column-level security) to enforce data governance policies across a multi-team data lake. / 3.	Build data quality validation into pipeline workflows using Glue Data Quality rules and implement alerting/quarantine patterns for data that fails validation. / 4.	Operationalize data pipelines with monitoring, error handling, retry logic, and cost optimization (right-sizing Glue DPUs, using Flex execution) for production reliability.

title: Introduction to EC2 Application Status Checks
description:
Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) now offers application status checks, a capability that lets you detect and respond to application health problems by monitoring your applications through configurable HTTP and HTTPS endpoints. Existing EC2 status checks monitor for reachability of the operating system, the underlying host, and EBS volumes.. If your application crashes but the instance stays up, those checks do not report a problem.
With application status checks, you configure an HTTP or HTTPS path and port, and the check is updated every 60 seconds. Results appear in the DescribeInstanceStatus API and Amazon CloudWatch alongside your existing status checks. When you pair application status checks with Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling, unhealthy instances are replaced.
In this course, you will learn how to create, associate, and manage application status checks so that you can monitor your applications and automatically replace unhealthy instances without manual intervention.

description:

description:

This course teaches you how to implement standardized communication protocols for AI agents using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. You will learn the Model Context Protocol (MCP) for universal AI-to-tool integration and the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol for inter-agent collaboration.

title: Introduction to AWS Resilience Migration Advisor Tool
description:

This course provides a comprehensive introduction to the AWS Resilience Migration Advisor (RMA), a locally guided facilitation tool built for strategic resilience planning and crisis response. The course begins by framing the challenge customers face during large scale events like a regional disruptions, potentially affecting more than one Availability Zone (AZ) — critical unknowns around where to move, how to move, who to call, and what steps to take — and then introduces RMA as the solution that eliminates planning paralysis and compresses hours of DR planning into minutes. Participants will explore RMA’s four operating modes across two primary paths: 

- Path A Execute Recovery Myself: With A1 Immediate DR Exit and A2 Architecture Strategy
- Path B Get Help from AWS Partners: With B1 Regional Partner Assistance and B2 Partner Matchmaking. 

The course covers Environment Discovery capability, target region selection including data residency and latency considerations, key AWS services supported for workload evacuation, and the comprehensive output packages generated by RMA including pre-evacuation checklists, prioritized action steps, exportable IaC configuration, and partner engagement briefs. 
Attendees will learn how to download, launch, and operate RMA across all paths, understand its positioning as an accelerator and facilitator (not an automated migration engine), and recognize its unique value for proactive resilience planning prior to a potential crisis response.
objectives: Understand the large scale event Challenge / Describe the Resilience Migration Advisor Tool:  / Navigate RMA’s two Primary paths and four Sub-Modes / Leverage the Environment Discovery Capability / Interpret RMA Output Packages:  / Apply RMA for Proactive Resilience Planning

title: Building Event-Driven Applications With Amazon EventBridge
description: Amazon EventBridge is a serverless event bus that makes it easy to connect applications together using data from customers applications, integrated software-as-a-service (SaaS) applications, and AWS services. You can use this service to build event-driven apps and route events from AWS services, or third-party apps or custom events that get created. In this course you will learn how to build event-driven applications by connecting multiple applications, including SaaS applications and AWS services, using the serverless event bus provided by Amazon EventBridge. This course includes the presentation of information, videos, demonstrations, and an assessment.
objectives: Describe the Amazon EventBridge features and use cases / Introduce Amazon EventBridge into an application design / Route Amazon EventBridge events using rules / Integrate Amazon EventBridge with other services / Explain best practices for using Amazon EventBridge / Describe how to achieve reliability with Amazon EventBridge / Discuss high-level security features of Amazon EventBridge

title: Introduction to AWS Lambda Web Functions
description: With AWS Lambda Web Functions, you can run web applications and API backends as serverless HTTP servers. Your code listens on a port and handles HTTP requests directly. You can use familiar Node.js web frameworks such as Express, Hono, or React Router. Lambda Web Functions manage execution environments and scales your application based on traffic, including to zero. Each endpoint provides an HTTPS domain with TLS. You choose whether Lambda authenticates callers with IAM (IamAuth) or your application handles authentication (ApplicationManaged). You deploy your code as a .zip file in a versioned Amazon S3 bucket without adapters or wrappers. By the end of this course, you will be able to describe how Lambda Web Functions run HTTP servers, create a Web Function and endpoint by using the Lambda console or the AWS CLI, and explain how revisions and revision weights support safe deployments and rollback.
aws_services: AWS Lambda

description:

title: Build with AgentCore Policy
description: Build with AgentCore Policy is a hands-on course that teaches you how to create, validate, test, and operate authorization policies for AI applications using Policy in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. You’ll work with Cedar policies, Policy Engines, AgentCore Gateway, natural-language policy generation, shadow testing, telemetry, time-based rules, and Guardrails while following a safe workflow for moving policies from development to enforcement.

title: QnABot on AWS
description: In this advanced-level course, you explore QnABot on AWS, a multi-channel, multi-language conversational chatbot powered by generative artificial intelligence (generative AI). You walk through the solution architecture, plan and launch a deployment in your own AWS account, and configure and operate the chatbot. You also diagnose the documented issues, update the stack, and uninstall the solution. This course is designed for cloud administrators, solutions architects, and contact center or chatbot owners.

title: Introduction to AWS Context
description:
An AI agent is only as intelligent as the context it can reason over. A capable model with no access to your data relationships, business rules, and domain knowledge will guess — and guesses are not decisions you can trust.

Today that context is scattered. It sits across data lakes, data warehouses, lakehouses, databases, and streams — and, just as often, in institutional knowledge that was never written down: which sources are authoritative, how tables join, what column "status" really means.

This course introduces AWS Context: enabling agents to have a safe, governed way to reach the context they need.

title: AWS File Storage Services Getting Started
description: Amazon Web Services (AWS) Storage provides the services you need to build the storage solution that's right for your organization. File storage services are one of the three primary types of storage in the AWS Storage portfolio. You will discover the file storage service options that are available to meet your organization's requirements. AWS file storage services include the Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) and Amazon FSx file systems. Amazon FSx includes the Amazon FSx for Windows File Server, Amazon FSx for Lustre, Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP, and Amazon FSx for OpenZFS file systems. You can select from these service offerings, apply them to your organization's needs, and determine the best storage solution. Before choosing an AWS storage solution, we recommend you first assess which storage characteristics are appropriate for your applications and business. After familiarizing yourself with AWS Storage, you can compare your requirements to the available AWS storage services and select the solution that meets your needs. In this course, you will learn about Amazon EFS and all four Amazon FSx file system services at an introductory level. You will learn about the architecture, use cases, and features of each of the services. This course includes: Online materials, demonstrations, and knowledge check questions.
objectives: Discuss available AWS file system storage services / Discuss the Amazon EFS service / Differentiate the Amazon FSx file systems from Amazon EFS / Discuss FSx for Windows File Server / Discuss FSx for Lustre / Discuss FSx for ONTAP / Discuss FSx for OpenZFS

Learners will discover how AWS invented Parallel-EAGLE (P-EAGLE), a breakthrough method that parallelizes speculative decoding for large language models on Amazon SageMaker AI. The course explains how traditional approaches like EAGLE generate draft tokens sequentially -- creating latency that grows with speculation depth -- and how P-EAGLE eliminates this bottleneck by predicting all draft tokens simultaneously in a single forward pass using learnable placeholders. title: Cloud Migration Factory on AWS
description: In this advanced-level course, you explore Cloud Migration Factory on AWS, a solution designed to coordinate and automate manual processes for large-scale migrations involving a substantial number of applications. It provides an orchestration platform for migrating workloads to AWS at scale. You walk through the solution architecture and its key components, then learn how to plan, deploy, and operate migrations while applying the solution's guidance for security, monitoring, and ongoing maintenance.

title: AWS CloudOps Engineer - Introduction to Cloud Operations
description:
This course introduces the concept of cloud operations and the role of the CloudOps engineer. The course also reviews the AWS Well-Architected Framework and explores the operational excellence pillar in depth. Finally, this course discusses the importance of tagging, specifically focusing on how a CloudOps engineer should consider implementing a tagging strategy.

This course is part of the [AWS CloudOps Engineer Learning Plan](https://skillbuilder.aws/learning-plan/BZJS8KQ916/aws-cloudops-engineer-learning-plan-includes-labs/8ZFKBMAMFH). If you are preparing for this role please refer to the other courses in the learning plan as needed.
objectives: Describe the fundamental tasks of the cloud operations cycle. / Identify the six pillars of the Well-Architected Framework. / Describe the components of the operational excellence pillar. / Explain how tagging is used in an AWS environment.

title: Introduction to Amazon OpenSearch optimized for log analytics
description: This course introduces Amazon OpenSearch Service optimized for log analytics, a new engine that delivers up to 4x improvement in price-performance for log analytics workloads. OpenSearch optimized for log analytics eliminates the traditional tradeoffs between cost, query speed, and full-text search depth that platform engineering and site reliability teams face as log volumes grow. The course covers core technical concepts, real-world use cases, performance characteristics, the customer experience for getting started, and how the optimized engine fits into the broader AWS analytics landscape. By the end of this course, you will understand when and why to use OpenSearch optimized for log analytics, how it performs under real workloads, and how to set up your first domain.

This course provides an in-depth exploration of AWS CloudTrail for security operations, incident response, and threat detection. The course begins with CloudTrail fundamentals, covering the architecture, event types (management, data, network activity, and insights events), and critical event fields essential for security investigations. Participants will learn to map common cloud attack patterns to the MITRE ATT&CK framework, understanding how adversaries operate in AWS environments through specific CloudTrail event sequences. The course demonstrates both traditional manual investigation techniques using CloudTrail Lake SQL queries and modern AI-powered approaches using Model Context Protocol (MCP) server tools. Through hands-on demonstrations with real-world use cases including compromised IAM credentials and S3 ransomware attacks, attendees will learn to conduct efficient security investigations by analyzing CloudTrail events, correlating multi-service activities, and leveraging AI agents to transform complex filtering and correlation tasks into natural language instructions. The training emphasizes practical skills for security analysts, SOC engineers, and incident responders who need to detect, investigate, and respond to security incidents in AWS environments.
objectives: Understand AWS CloudTrail Fundamentals / Analyze CloudTrail Event Structure / Map Attack Patterns to MITRE ATT&CK Framework / Conduct Security Investigations with CloudTrail Lake / Leverage CloudTrail MCP Server Tools / Apply Practical Investigation Techniques

Learners will discover how to move beyond traditional supervisor-based multi-agent architectures by exploring self-organizing agent clusters that coordinate through shared state rather than central orchestration.
